prompt: Our NestJS API serves portfolio funds. v2 renamed currency to baseCurrency and moved the flat cashPct into liquidity.cashPct alongside a new liquidity.hqlaPct (default 0). Mobile clients pinned to v1 can't redeploy quickly. Using @skew/contract, write: (1) the contract document JSON for portfolio-fund, (2) the Nest controller that publishes it at the well-known URL with proper caching, and (3) the client-side code a v1 app uses to read a v2 response body without breaking, labeling what it loses.
assertions: Contract JSON has skewContract: "1", name, current: 2, and a steps array with from/to numbers
Every op in the document comes from the closed whitelist (rename, move, wrap, hoist, map, default, drop, convert, const) — no executable code in the document
The step uses rename for currency->baseCurrency, move for cashPct->liquidity.cashPct, and default for liquidity.hqlaPct = 0
Controller serves GET .well-known/skew/contracts/:name with an ETag derived from contractFingerprint(doc) and returns 304 when if-none-match matches
Controller sets cache-control no-cache (revalidate) rather than long-lived caching or no header
Client pins its schema with versionedFromContract<FundV1>(contract, { at: 1 }) or equivalent pinned construction
Client reads via createContractResolver().readResolving(...) against the well-known URL so 'ahead' data is cured by fetching the contract
Loss is surfaced: code inspects/reports downgradedFrom and lossyPaths rather than silently returning the projection
